header.text: Chapter 04 · How to read this reading
The chart is fixed. The reading is a tradition.
Four Pillars is a structural language before it is anything else. This chapter explains what the report does with it, what it leaves out, and how to tell one from the other on every page.

blocks.text: A BaZi chart is not a verdict written about you. It is eight characters, four Heavenly Stems above four Earthly Branches, set out in four columns for the year, month, day and hour of a birth. They come from a calendar system used in China for well over two thousand years, and the arrangement itself is mechanical: given a moment and a declared day boundary, the eight characters are fixed. Two people born in the same hour in the same place receive the same eight.

What follows from those characters is a different matter, and that difference is why this report is built the way it is. The chart facts are deterministic. The reading is interpretation, a tradition of relating the characters to one another, developed over centuries, with schools that disagree. Bazodiac keeps the two visibly apart rather than blending them into one confident voice. Chart pages carry a provenance line naming where their values came from. Reading pages are marked as reading.

Every character on a chart page is set as real text in a real typeface, never drawn and never generated. Where one appears large, it also appears complete: a Stem or a Branch is never cropped for effect. Pinyin always carries its tone marks, because without them a syllable is ambiguous. A Branch is never swapped for its animal. The animal is a traditional association that travels with the Branch, and it is shown as a secondary label so that the character remains the fact and the animal remains the association.

Colour is used sparingly and always locally. A field of colour classifies exactly one thing at a time: this Stem, that Branch, this one Hidden Stem. A whole pillar is never tinted, because a pillar holds a Stem and a Branch that usually belong to different phases, and a single wash over both would be a claim the chart does not make. The Day Master is set apart with a quiet gold edge on a neutral ground. Gold is a selection, not a sixth phase.
Everything marked Your chart came from validated chart data. Everything marked General education is identical in every copy.
What this edition deliberately leaves out

Some things are absent on purpose. This edition does not calculate the strength of a Day Master, does not nominate a favourable element, does not draw luck pillars or annual transits, and prints no lucky numbers, colours or directions. None of that is an oversight. Each would require a method this report has not committed to, and printing it anyway would mean asserting something the report cannot support. Where a page shows a count, the count is a count: a zero in the Wu Xing distribution means the tally is zero, not that something is missing from you.

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: Read the chart pages and the reading pages as two different kinds of writing. One reports what your chart contains. The other explains a system that existed long before your chart did. Where the two meet, the page says so.

That restraint has a cost and a benefit. The cost is that you will not find a sentence telling you what will happen. The benefit is that everything you do find can be traced, either to a character in your chart, to a named relationship between characters, or to a labelled piece of general education. If a passage cannot be traced to one of those, it does not belong in this document, and it is not here.
How the following chapters are built

Each interpretive chapter opens with the part of the chart it refers to, named in the running head, so you always know which characters a passage is about. A short highlighted sentence marks the one idea the chapter turns on. A Key insight panel, where present, restates the practical point in plain words. Chapters are written to be read in order, but each one stands on its own, and nothing in a later chapter overrides an earlier one.

You may find that some passages describe you well and others do not. That is expected, and it is not a failure of the chart or of you. A classical reading describes a structure and the tendencies traditionally associated with it. What you do with a structure is the part that stays yours. If you want to go further, the method note at the end of this report states which conventions were used and which were deliberately left aside.
